security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are documentation syntax, placeholder credentials, or non-executable examples. The skill performs explicit documentation fetches and local commands, while the evaluation harness can launch caller-selected processes and does not enforce its read-only policy. No malicious intent or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: The evaluation harness does not enforce read-only tool use.
remediation.suggestion: Filter tools by trustworthy read-only annotations and require confirmation before any state-changing or unclassified tool call.

remediation.issue: The stdio evaluator launches any command supplied by its caller.
remediation.suggestion: Display the executable and arguments, require explicit confirmation, and reject command values from untrusted or automated input.

remediation.issue: The workflow fetches mutable protocol and SDK documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin SDK references to reviewed releases or commit hashes, and treat fetched text as untrusted reference material.

content.value_statement: MCP server design requires careful tool schemas, integrations, and evaluation. This skill guides Python and TypeScript implementations from research through testing.
actual_capabilities: Guides workflow-focused MCP tool selection and planning.
Provides Python FastMCP and TypeScript SDK implementation patterns.
Explains input validation, pagination, truncation, errors, and tool annotations.
Includes an evaluation harness for stdio, SSE, and streamable HTTP servers.
Shows how to create stable, read-only evaluation questions and reports.
limitations: It does not verify that a service API or generated integration is correct.
Current protocol, SDK, and service research requires network access.
The evaluation harness uses the Anthropic API and requires a valid key.
Generated servers and third-party dependencies still require independent security review.

use_cases.title: Plan an API integration
use_cases.description: Turn service documentation into a focused MCP tool plan with authentication, pagination, and response requirements.

use_cases.title: Implement a typed server
use_cases.description: Build a Python or TypeScript MCP server with validated inputs, shared helpers, and useful errors.

use_cases.title: Evaluate tool quality
use_cases.description: Create stable questions, run the included harness, and review accuracy, latency, tool usage, and model feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a first MCP server
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an MCP server for [service]. Review its API needs and propose focused tools, authentication, pagination, errors, and response formats. Do not implement yet.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a documented service API.

prompt_templates.title: Build with Python FastMCP
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Python FastMCP server for [service] using [authentication method]. Include validated inputs, async requests, pagination, concise outputs, errors, and read-only annotations.

prompt_templates.title: Build with TypeScript
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a strict TypeScript MCP server for [service]. Use Zod schemas, shared API helpers, typed errors, pagination, annotations, and a working build setup.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and evaluate a server
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my MCP server in [path] against the included guides. Identify security and usability gaps, fix them, then create ten stable read-only evaluations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review and evaluation of an existing server.

output_examples.input: Plan an MCP server for a project management API.
output: A prioritized tool list centered on common project workflows.
Authentication, pagination, validation, and error-handling requirements.
A staged implementation and evaluation plan.

output_examples.input: Review a Python FastMCP server with large search responses.
output: Findings covering missing limits, weak schemas, and inconsistent errors.
Recommended pagination, truncation, and concise response options.
A focused checklist for implementation and testing.

output_examples.input: Create evaluations for a read-only issue tracker server.
output: Ten independent questions with stable, verifiable answers.
Coverage across search, filtering, aggregation, and cross-tool workflows.
Instructions for running the harness and reviewing its report.

best_practices: Design tools around complete user workflows instead of mirroring every API endpoint.
Validate all inputs and return concise, actionable errors with recovery guidance.
Review fetched documentation, local commands, tool permissions, and dependencies before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not expose destructive tools to an unattended evaluation agent.
Do not return unbounded API responses or large raw payloads.
Do not place real credentials in prompts, examples, source files, or reports.

faq.question: Which implementation languages are supported?
faq.answer: The guides cover Python with FastMCP and Node or TypeScript with the MCP SDK.

faq.question: Does the workflow require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks the agent to fetch current protocol, SDK, and service API documentation.

faq.question: Does the skill run local commands?
faq.answer: The workflow may run syntax checks, builds, and the evaluation harness. Review commands and project dependencies before execution.

faq.question: How should API keys be supplied?
faq.answer: The examples use placeholders. Supply real keys through trusted environment or header settings, and never commit them.

faq.question: What does the evaluation harness measure?
faq.answer: It reports answer accuracy, task duration, tool-call counts, execution summaries, and model feedback.

faq.question: Does this skill guarantee a secure server?
faq.answer: No. Generated integrations, permissions, dependencies, and remote services require independent security review before deployment.
